constraints: Use Python only — pydeseq2, not R DESeq2 and not rpy2.

steps.description: Run pydeseq2 on the aligned raw integer counts with design ~condition, setting control as the reference level so positive log2 fold changes mean higher in AD lesional. steps.name: Hallmark GSEA on the AD-vs-control ranking
caveats: If the human hallmark collection cannot be resolved at run time, do not substitute the mouse hallmark or an oncogenic/GO collection as a stand-in — report the gap explicitly and fall back to the staged human GO BP collection only as a clearly labelled substitute that answers a different question.

With ~12,000 genes tested, several hallmark sets will be represented by a reduced fraction of their members; report the post-restriction set size beside every result and treat sets that lost most members as uninterpretable.

Hallmark sets overlap in membership (inflammatory response, TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB, IL6_JAK_STAT3, interferon sets share genes); correlated hits are not independent findings and should be summarised as one inflammatory block rather than counted separately.
GSEA on n=6 per group inherits the DE model's power limits — an FDR<0.25 hit is a hypothesis, not a result, and must be labelled that way.
steps.context: Input is a ranked gene list of human gene symbols from a 6v6 AD-lesional-vs-control skin contrast, not a count matrix — hence the enrichment agent rather than the transcriptomics agent. The environment stages an MSigDB human hallmark symbols GMT (50 sets) alongside a mouse hallmark file and human GO/oncogenic collections; the human hallmark file is the one this step requires, and the organism must be matched explicitly since a mouse GMT would silently produce near-empty overlaps. The research question asks specifically for hallmark pathways, so hallmark is primary; GO BP may be added only as an optional secondary annotation if time permits, clearly labelled as supplementary.
steps.question: Which MSigDB hallmark pathways are coordinately up- or down-regulated in AD lesional skin versus control, and are those pathway calls robust to exclusion of the shallow sample_01?
constraints: Use Python only — gseapy (and/or decoupler), not R clusterProfiler or fgsea.

Resolve the human hallmark gene set collection from the environment's reference data at run time and print the resolved path and the number of sets parsed; confirm the file is the Homo sapiens hallmark collection before using it.

Restrict every gene set to the tested gene universe from T1S2 before computing set sizes and before the ORA background — the input matrix carries only 12,000 genes, so unrestricted set sizes and an all-genes background would both inflate significance.
Set a fixed random seed and report the permutation count so the GSEA result is reproducible.
Report NES with FDR q for all 50 hallmark sets, not only the significant ones, so the absence of a pathway is interpretable.
Run the prerank a second time on the sample_01-excluded ranking and report the overlap of significant sets between the two.
steps.description: Run pre-ranked gene set enrichment on the DE ranking from T1S2 against the human hallmark gene set collection — 50 HALLMARK_* sets keyed on HGNC gene symbols — resolved from the environment's staged reference data for Homo sapiens (the human hallmark GMT, not the mouse one). acceptance_criteria: The resolved human hallmark GMT path and the number of gene sets parsed are printed; organism is confirmed human.
A full table of all hallmark sets with NES, nominal p, FDR q, set size after universe restriction, and leading-edge genes is written for the primary ranking.
Significant sets are reported at both FDR < 0.25 and FDR < 0.05, split by direction of NES.
The hypergeometric ORA cross-check on padj<0.05 up and down DE genes is reported with the T1S2 tested universe as background.
GSEA enrichment plots and an NES bar plot are saved.
A sensitivity comparison table lists hallmark sets significant in the full fit, the 11-sample fit, or both.

plan.title: AD lesional vs control DE + hallmark GSEA (Python)
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single-batch bulk RNA-seq experiment in human skin: a 12,000 gene x 12 sample raw Salmon count matrix (counts.csv, gene symbols in the first column) with a 12-row metadata.csv giving one condition per sample — 6 atopic dermatitis lesional vs 6 control, unpaired. The research question is two-part: which genes change, and which hallmark pathways change; plus an explicit instruction to handle the shallow sample carefully. Everything is written in Python (user constraint: no R), which the environment supports fully — pydeseq2 0.5.4 for the negative-binomial DE model and gseapy 1.3.1 for GSEA/ORA, both confirmed present.

The profile flags sample_01 at roughly 4x below median library depth. That is the one methodological fork in this plan, so it is resolved with evidence rather than by assumption: T1S1 quantifies depth, detected-gene count, and the sample's position in PCA/correlation space after variance-stabilising transformation, and writes an explicit keep/drop recommendation. A 4x depth deficit alone is NOT grounds for exclusion — DESeq2's size-factor normalisation and dispersion model absorb depth differences, and dropping a sample from a 6v6 design costs real power. It becomes grounds for exclusion only if sample_01 is also an expression outlier (few detected genes, poor correlation with its own group, separating on PC1 in a direction that tracks depth rather than condition). T1S2 therefore runs the primary DESeq2 contrast on all 12 samples and re-runs it with sample_01 removed as a sensitivity analysis, reporting the concordance of the two gene lists. That way the shallow sample changes the confidence attached to a hit, not the existence of the analysis.

T2S1 takes the shrunk-LFC-ranked gene list into hallmark GSEA against the staged MSigDB human hallmark collection (50 HALLMARK_* sets, HGNC symbols — the correct organism file, matching the human skin data). Ranked GSEA is the right test here rather than a threshold-based ORA over DE genes, because it uses the whole ranking and does not inherit the p-value cutoff; an ORA on the significant set is run alongside only as a cross-check. The hallmark result is also recomputed on the sensitivity ranking so that no reported pathway rests solely on the full-cohort ranking if sample_01 drove it. Expected biology for AD lesional skin (type-2/IL-13 inflammation, keratinocyte proliferation, interferon and TNF/NF-kB signalling, barrier gene loss) is stated as a prior for sanity-checking the direction of results, not as a target to confirm.

Caveats carried through the whole plan: n=6 per group is modest, the matrix is pre-filtered to 12,000 genes so absolute pathway coverage is reduced relative to a full transcriptome and the GSEA background must be the tested universe, and 'treated' in the research question means the AD lesional group — this is a disease-vs-control contrast, not a drug treatment, so no exposure-response or pharmacological interpretation applies.
